descriptions.description: Isolated from the symptomatic branch of Heptapleurum heptaphyllum (L.) Y. F. Deng (Araliaceae). Sexual morph: Undetermined. Asexual morph: Conidiomata pycnidial, globose, dark brown, superficial on PDA, releasing conidia in a yellow mass, slimy. Conidiophores pale brown, smooth-walled, septate, unbranched, (13 –) 16 – 43 (– 44) × (3 –) 4 – 5 (– 5.5) μm (mean ± SD = 24 ± 1 × 4 ± 0.5 μm). Conidiogenous cells hyaline to pale brown, smooth-walled, cylindrical to ampulliform, flask-shaped, (9.3 –) 10 – 19 (– 20) × (3.4 –) 4 – 5 (– 5.3) μm (mean ± SD = 15 ± 1 × 4 ± 0.3 μm), at collarette 1 – 2 μm (width). Setae brown to dark brown, smooth-walled to finely verruculose, 2 – 4 septate, (30 –) 50 – 70 (– 100) µm long, base cylindrical to conical, 4 – 6 (– 9) µm diam., tip acute to roundish. Conidia (14 –) 15 – 19 (– 21) × (5.5 –) 5.8 – 6 (– 7) μm (mean ± SD = 16 ± 1 × 6 ± 0.2 μm), n = 60, L / W ratio = 2.8, hyaline, aseptate, smooth-walled, ellipsoidal to cylindrical, one end rounded and one end acute or both ends rounded, guttulate, granular. Appressoria absent. Culture characteristics: Colony on PDA reaching 7 – 8 cm diam after 7 d at room temperature (± 25 ° C), under light 12 hr / dark 12 hr, colonies rhizoid to filamentous, flat surface, with filiform margin, pale grey or grey-green from above and white to pale-gray reverse, producing grouped pycnidia with raised mycelium surrounded. Colonies on CMA reaching 7 – 8 cm diam after 7 d at room temperature (± 25 ° C), under light 12 hr / dark 12 hr, colonies rhizoid to filamentous, dense, flat or raised surface, with filiform margin, white from above and white to pale-yellow reverse, with producing grouped-pycnidia. Colonies on WA with sterilized sticks, reaching 5 cm diam after 7 d at room temperature (± 25 ° C), under light 12 hr / dark 12 hr, colonies rhizoid to filamentous, dense, flat surface, with filiform margin, dark green from above and reverse, with producing pycnidia on sticks and immersed pycnidia under media.

Notes: Based on morphological characteristics and multi-locus phylogenetic analyses, Colletotrichum guttulatum is a distinct clade within the C. dracaenophilum species complex. Colletotrichum guttulatum forms a sister clade to C. coelogynes, C. crousii, C. parallelophorum, and other closely related taxa (Figure 1), with support of 82 % maximum likelihood bootstrap values and 0.99 Bayesian posterior probabilities. Morphologically, C. guttulatum shares common characteristics with other species in the complex, including hyaline, smooth-walled, aseptate, straight, cylindrical conidia with rounded apices and bases. However, it is distinguishable from its closest relatives by subtle differences in conidial dimensions: (14 –) 15 – 19 (– 21) × (5.5 –) 5.8 – 6 (– 7) μm in C. guttulatum versus (15 –) 15.5 – 18 (– 20) × (4.5 –) 5 – 6 (– 6.5) μm in C. coelogynes, 12.5 – 18.5 × 6.5 – 8 μm in C. crousii, and (12.1 –) 13.8 – 16.8 (– 18.9) × (3.3 –) 4.4 – 7.5 (– 7.9) µm in C. parallelophorum (Ma et al. 2018, Liu et al. 2022). The conidia of C. guttulatum are slightly longer and narrower in comparison. Pairwise nucleotide comparisons of Colletotrichum dracaenophilum with C. coelogynes, C. crousii, and C. parallelophorum revealed consistent genetic differences across all loci. The observed differences include: ITS: 3 % (17 / 541), 5 % (27 / 533), and 4 % (15 / 433) with 2, 7, and 3 gaps, respectively; act: 7.5 % (21 / 277), 7 % (17 / 255), no data for C. parallelophorum; 5, 3, and no gaps; gapdh: 16 % (44 / 285), 16 % (46 / 281), and 22 % (57 / 259) with 6, 4, and 14 gaps; β-tubulin: 7 % (37 / 534), 8 % (57 / 704), and 7.3 % (33 / 455) with 1, 8, and 1 gap; chs- 1: 2 % (6 / 300), 3.6 % (11 / 300), no gaps; his 3: 8.7 % (34 / 393), 9 % (35 / 392) with 2 and 3 gaps, respectively. Colletotrichum coelogynes and C. crousii do not contain the cal gene, whereas C. parallelophorum lacks the act, chs- 1, his 3, and cal genes. These molecular differences, particularly the high variation observed across multiple loci, provide strong evidence for the taxonomic separation of C. dracaenophilum from its relatives. In addition to morphological and phylogenetic evidence, the pairwise homoplasy index (PHI) test showed no significant signs of recombination between C. guttulatum and its phylogenetically closest relatives, C. coelogynes, C. crousii, and C. parallelophorum (Φw = 0.9942; Figure 2), supporting its genetic distinctiveness. The combination of phylogenetic support, clear morphological differentiation, and the absence of recombination provides robust evidence for recognizing C. guttulatum as a novel species within the C. dracaenophilum species complex.
Etymology: refers to the guttulate nature of the conidia, “ bearing guttules ”

Living in Taiwan in leaf galls of Heptapleurum arboricola (possible spelling error in plant name, Wang & Lin 2020: 361), this species has an unusual pelta with no CPS but bearing 3 – 4 tiny setae posterolaterally (Fig. 72). From Yunnan, 17 females and 6 males on leaves or leaf galls of plants labelled as Schefflera heptaphylla and S. octophylla are here recognized from China. The host plant name Schefflera heptaphylla is more validly Heptapleurum heptaphyllum as the genus Heptapleurum was distinguished from Schefflera in 2020 and accepted by Plants of the World Online (Lowry et al. 2020; POWO 2023). Moreover, Schefflera octophylla is a synonym of H. heptaphyllum (IPNI 2023).

Comments. As indicated above, Takahashi described this species from specimens taken on leaves of Heptapleurinum arboricolum (= Schefflera arboricola) at Sozan near Taihoku. Specimens deposited in TARI have the same data as with the original type description, and these specimens are here assumed to be syntypes. Takahashi pointed out that this species differs from heptapleurinus in two insignificant characters: colour of the leaf galls and shapes of the mouth cone (Takahashi 1937). Our further studies showed that these two species can be distinguished as follows: heptapleuricola po setae about 0.5 as long as dorsal length of eyes; pronotal am setae shorter than aa setae; pelta without CPS but with setae present laterally. In contrast, heptapleurinus po setae are longer than eyes; pronotal am setae are longer than aa setae; pelta is with CPS but without setae laterally.

Female macroptera. Body length 2.1 – 2.3 mm. Color brown; antennal segments I and II brown, same colour as head, except distal portion of II yellowish, III – VI and basal 1 / 3 of VII yellow, most of VII and VIII greyish brown; all femora brown, fore tibiae yellow, mid and hind tibiae brown, except apices yellow, all tarsi yellow; fore wings pale brown with a darker stripe; major body setae brown. Head 1.3 times as long as wide (Fig. 35), with regular reticulation on dorsum anterior to and between eyes, followed by transverse reticles; cheeks with 3 – 4 pairs of short setae, po setae blunt, shorter than length of eyes; maxillary stylets retracted to level of po setae, about 1 / 5 of head width apart; mouth cone wide and rounded (Fig. 36); antennal segment III 1.5 times, segment IV 1.3 times as long as II (Fig. 42). Pronotum with 5 pairs of major setae (Fig. 37), all blunt, aa setae longer than am setae, shorter than other pairs; mesopresternum boat shape, some with irregular margins (Fig. 39); metanotal sculpture dense and longitudinal; fore wing with 11 – 15 duplicated cilia. Pelta triangular, 2 – 4 short setae on each side (Fig. 38), CPS absent; tergite II laterally with 3 – 4 accessary setae (Fig. 40), tube straight-sided, about same length as head (Fig. 41). Male macroptera. Body length 1.8 – 2.0 mm; colour and shape similar to female. Specimens examined. Taiwan, Taihoku (Taipei), Syntype 16 females, 7 males, from leave galls of Heptapleurinum arboricolum, 31. x. 1936 (Takahashi); 15 females, 5 males, Lianhuachi (Nantou), from Schefflera arboricola, 27. ix. 1992.
